items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1976-02-04
items.q: And Professor Cook was the emcee in musical and performance director and everything. He was the wheel around there. So he staged this train excursion to Chicago, and we had our band to play.

ctx.x: Excuse me Danny, what was the name of the band you were with then?

I was with Lee Collins, Jones and Collins. Astoria Band. We played at Astoria. We played in New Orleans on Rampart Street which was owned by Beansy Furrier. It had once been owned by, I can't think of a man's name. It was a brewery people. Beansy took it over. It was a gambling concession. and we worked there. And Professor Cook was the emcee in musical and performance director and everything. He was the wheel around there. So he staged this train excursion to Chicago, and we had our band to play. items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That was Professor Cook. Doc Cook was a man who had different degrees

ctx.x: What was Professor Cook’s first name?

Professor Cook? I don’t know his first. It’ll come to me, but I ain’t, we ain’t go time to find it. It’s two different Cooks. One couldn’t read no music and barely could read and write. That was Professor Cook. Doc Cook was a man who had different degrees from music, higher bred and higher learned and highly calculated. He ended up going to New York City and was a staff arranger for NBC.
How long did you play in Chicago?
